metadata.method_name: plan-subspace projection vs random plan-site pushes (Qwen3-8B)
metadata.description: See README.md; every number here is recomputed by audit/rederive.py.

excluded: exp13 iter1-3, sham (prompt text not on record here)
exp13 rand1-3 (push directions not on record)
exp7 / exp6 T1/T2 novelty, mention, seeds (no outcomes)

departure.note: exp16 reports F_direct pooled over its 5 route tasks, not per task

R2_prediction.note: committed prediction for a future R2 ban (no R2 ban was rendered)

novelty.claim: no correct novel algorithm among the correct push programs

unit_tests_gpu.CLAMP_note: criterion in the plan: < 1e-3; the edited state is cast back to the block dtype (bf16), whose rounding (~2^-8 relative per coordinate) bounds the achievable residual

labeller_recheck.note: mechanical labels only (runtime/AST); the judge is not re-run (spend)

deviations.what: FP8 (E4M3) W8A8-dynamic decoder linears instead of bf16, B = 20 for every task
deviations.why: 16 GB RTX 2000 Ada; this is the plan's own S0.1 row for a 16 GB Ada GPU (bf16 weights need 16.4 GB)
deviations.consequence: same numerics as the iteration-3 exp17 screen; the engine check reproduced 180/180 screen slots with identical code sha256 (results/engine_check.json)

deviations.what: max_new = 1024 for T1/T2 (plan: 1536 for bf16 path rows)
deviations.why: keeps the exp17 screen engine exactly (its T1/T2 rows used 1024) and the B = 20 prealloc in memory
deviations.consequence: rows hitting the limit are 'length'; the labeller still extracts an unterminated block

deviations.what: bench pushes use the plan's ban unit (exp13 bf16 norms), which is 9-16% smaller than exp17's FP8 norms on T03/T04/T05/T06 (results/units.json)
deviations.why: plan S2.9 names exp13 norms for bench tasks
deviations.consequence: bench population pushes are ~10-16% weaker than the screen pushes of the same alpha; the engine check used exp17's norms to replicate the screen

deviations.what: T1/T2 named prompts = the bench forced_templates x (exp7 display name + two hand-written aliases)
deviations.why: no alias lists exist for T1/T2; exp7's 'forced|X|plain|kN' prompts equal these for 2 of 10 templates per mode (prompts/prompts4_report.json)
deviations.consequence: same structure as the bench named prompts

deviations.what: T1/T2 masked prompts built like the bench ones (10 frames x 3 leak-checked descriptions) instead of exp7's 'desc' prompts
deviations.why: exp7's desc prompts contain the algorithm name and fail the alias-leak check
deviations.consequence: 0 masked prompts leak a name on any task

deviations.what: commit #1 (before the first population sample) holds every predictor value, all reading rules verbatim, the screen hash and the PRIMARY analysis code (analysis/common.py, c2a.py, tests); decomp.py and c2c.py were chained as addendum 1 before their arms were sampled, and c2b/geometry/novelty/c3b/run_all as addendum 2 before they were run
deviations.why: writing all seven analysis files before sampling would have left the GPU idle for ~1 h of a 6 h budget
deviations.consequence: commitments.log keeps the order; corrections of committed files are new entries (supersede by path)

deviations.what: C2b uses exp13 nonce/novelty/ban/bandpatch rows (12 bench tasks) and exp17 BAN and RAND rows (T03-T06, T1, T2); the ITER1 exp6 T1/T2 seeds and outcomes are not on disk (purged), and exp13 rand1-3 directions are not on record
deviations.consequence: C2b covers 14 tasks with prompt knobs and 6 with push knobs

deviations.what: arms of one (task, template) are packed into shared 20-row batches (twin with population; decomposition with the C2c core; C2c extras with the sweep); leftover rows are padded with extra twin slots k >= 10
deviations.consequence: none on CRN coupling: decode is row-position independent at B = 20 (U1b passed); extra twin rows are reported apart

deviations.what: the plan's 'H5, P15 and P20 on the randomisation hull' are not defined in the inputs; reported instead: the best dose on the hull {twin, s doses} by correct-only Hill subject to pass within 5 points, with linear interpolation between doses as a sensitivity
the departure rule reports exp16's F_direct pooled over its 5 route tasks
opening-ladder openings reconstruct the '```python' fence before the forced programs' extracted code
deviations.why: only the extracted code is on record

deviations.what: AST 4-gram phrasing clusters are computed for arms with <= 120 correct programs
deviations.consequence: large twin-like arms have no cluster count

budget_decision.note: B continues for all movable tasks (never drop); later stages are checked against the deadline in the committed drop order
